lines.cap: She was with hundreds of men, right at the very end. And they all said the same thing.
lines.say: She was with hundreds of men, right at the very end. And they all said the same thing.

lines.cap: Bronnie Ware was a palliative carer in Australia. She looked after people in their last weeks of life.
lines.say: Bronnie Ware was a palliative carer in Australia. She looked after people in their last weeks of life.

lines.cap: She asked them what they regretted. The answers kept repeating.
lines.say: She asked them what they regretted. The answers kept repeating.

lines.cap: Every man she nursed said, I wish I hadn't worked so hard.
lines.say: Every man she nursed said, I wish I hadn't worked so hard.

lines.cap: Others wished they'd had the courage to live their own life, not the one others expected.
lines.say: Others wished they'd had the courage to live their own life, not the one others expected.

lines.cap: To say how they really felt. To stay in touch with friends.
lines.say: To say how they really felt. To stay in touch with friends.

lines.cap: And to let themselves be happier. Many only realised at the end that happiness was a choice.
lines.say: And to let themselves be happier. Many only realised at the end that happiness was a choice.

lines.cap: So log off. Call someone. You still have time.
lines.say: So log off. Call someone. You still have time.
